item.title: Proton-Coupled Electrostatic Regulation of Anion Electrosorption in Electric Double Layers
item.description:

Journal of the American Chemical Society | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in using anodic polarization to create a depth-graded TiO2–x architecture whose internal electric field drives subsurface proton accumulation, electrostatically regulating anion electrosorption and lateral anion interactions. A thin crystalline anatase surface extends the anodic operating range. This enables 3.0 V aqueous supercapacitors in Na2SO4 over 45,000 cycles and 2.7 V in seawater, establishing subsurface ionic chemistry as a design variable.

item.title: Regulating Functionalized MXene Crystal-Field Splitting toward Efficient Bifunctional Oxygen Electrocatalysis of Lithium–Oxygen Batteries
item.description:

Journal of the American Chemical Society | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This study pioneers crystal-field splitting engineering at Ti sites in MXenes as a predictive electronic descriptor for bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysis. By weakening Ti ligand fields through anionic/cationic modification, it enhances electron delocalization, enabling asymmetric Li₂O₂ adsorption and lower ORR/OER barriers. Cu–Ti₃C₂Br₂ achieves 11,662 mAh g⁻¹ capacity and 50% reduced overpotential, establishing a rational design strategy for lithium–oxygen battery catalysts.
🏷 lithium-oxygen battery · MXene · crystal-field splitting · oxygen electrocatalysis · Ti3C2

This yields 1.02 mS cm−1 ionic conductivity at 25 °C and stable all-solid-state battery cycling for 850 cycles, offering a practical, low-cost route to high-performance sodium batteries.

💡 The novelty lies in a temperature–pressure dual-signal coupling sensor that detects coupled precursors within battery packs, flagging abnormalities ~40 min before thermal runaway. item.title: Engineering Amino‐Induced p‐π Conjugation for Electronic Regulation of Li + Transport in PVDF‐Based Solid‐State Electrolytes
item.description:

Angewandte Chemie International Edition | 🔬 Research Article
💡 Amino-functionalized UiO66-NH₂ in PVDF/LiFSI induces p-π conjugation and enhanced ligand-to-metal charge transfer, reshaping the electrostatic landscape to weaken Li⁺-FSI⁻ pairing. This yields high ionic conductivity (2.41×10⁻³ S cm⁻¹), Li⁺ transference number 0.56, and stable high-loading NCM811 cycling, establishing electronic-structure engineering of MOF fillers as a novel route to high-performance solid-state electrolytes.
🏷 PVDF electrolyte · UiO66-NH2 · p-π conjugation · Li+ transport · solid-state battery

💡 The novelty lies in molecular design-enabled electronic structure engineering to reconfigure the interfacial electrochemical environment, using dual-axis screening of electron-donating capability and molecular asymmetry. item.description:
